claims.text: A refined grain architecture with a continuous intergranular oxide or intermetallic network governs simultaneous wear and corrosion resistance in refractory high-entropy alloys.
The refined intergranular architecture improves wear resistance through strain hardening and grain-boundary reinforcement.
Intergranular oxides or intermetallic precipitates improve corrosion resistance by promoting a stable passive film.
The proposed initial alloy can be synthesized by powder metallurgy and spark plasma sintering.
The spark-plasma-sintered alloy has a BCC solid-solution matrix.
The alloy contains Laves phases and oxides, with at least some precipitation occurring at grain boundaries.
Lower sintering temperatures produce finer BCC grains than higher sintering temperatures.
Lower sintering temperatures produce a more continuous protective grain-boundary precipitate network.
Increasing the sintering temperature to 1400 °C causes coarsening of the BCC grains.
Increasing the sintering temperature decreases the Laves-phase content.
Grain-boundary oxides or intermetallic phases impede crack propagation during wear.
Grain-boundary precipitates provide sites for formation of a stable passive layer.
Grain refinement increases alloy strength through grain-boundary strengthening.
The integrated refined and precipitate-bearing microstructure reduces material loss by resisting mechanical deformation.
The integrated microstructure lowers electrochemical attack rates by maintaining a protective passive layer.
The fine-grained sample with a continuous intergranular network will have a lower wear rate than the composition-matched coarse-grained baseline.
The fine-grained sample with a continuous intergranular network will have a lower corrosion current density than the composition-matched coarse-grained baseline.
The beneficial effect should disappear when mechanical stresses exceed passive-layer adhesion strength or when aggressive pH or chloride concentrations disrupt passivation.
Prior evidence shows that the CrMoNbWV alloy has high wear resistance and high corrosion resistance in sulfuric-acid electrochemical testing.
Prior evidence establishes that grain refinement and precipitate formation enhance the separate wear and corrosion properties.
